title: What you think of the idea ,the current progress and the plan?
author: PossibleAnteater4062
selftext:
Disclaimer I am running this on potato if wondering.  So in my own words my plan with this is the following. A tool that makes your workflow much more streamline by visual design as i want certain tech behind it example imagine you seamlessly alter the terrains texture and make terrain to something realistic if don't like what about trees you want take them away or add better one with higher quality what about a building u want better looking one ask ai to improve it all these with slider and tools the Ai can even use even better tech for landscape and procuderal generations hook it up with Ai pathing and rpg system so now Npc can walk around map you see and visualize through tool so now Ai can explain it .....

What Valley Studio can build today

Valley Studio is P300’s workspace for building and playtesting RPG environments inside Godot. You can plan a settlement from above, adjust the landscape around it, then take control of the hero and walk through the result.

\- Terrain and routes. Lay out roads, rivers, ridges, and terrace areas. Rebuild the terrain, inspect steepness and walkability, and wipe between two versions to see where the ground changed.

\- Settlements and landmarks. Review locations such as the smithy, inn, and mill through their place cards, building specs, and production status. The mill crossing is a built example with a bridge, stone weir, and C++-generated paddle wheel.

\- Materials and vegetation. Inspect habitats and preview how water, exposure, and land use affect the blend of soil, rock, and river sediment. Review proposed cedar, oak, and bamboo placement against roads, fields, and buildings.

\- Dungeon layouts. Compare seeded cave and ruin candidates, trace the route from entrance to key to goal, and see why a layout failed. The current review checks the layout grid. A playable dungeon still needs a 3D collision and interaction pass.

Why it works well for AI agents

An agent can read actual slope, water depth, and route measurements, propose an edit, and see what needs to rebuild before applying it. The live Studio and headless runner accept the same structured operations. Changes can be logged, compared, and undone.

For example, if you ask for a gentler road to the ford, an agent can measure the current grade, test a new alignment on a copy, and show you the grade, earthwork, and camera views for both routes. You make the design call with the evidence in front of you.

Where it goes next

1. Make generation repeatable. Protect hand-built locations, doors, and crossings when the surrounding terrain or vegetation regenerates. Start with the ford and smithy.

2. Expand the building tools. Add a searchable asset shelf, snapping, placement checks, in-world notes, and fuller AI controls for reviewing multiple candidates.

3. Connect the living world. Make NPC schedules, trade, and factions respond to persistent events. A missed rice delivery could change shop stock, delay work, and still matter when the player returns.

4. Build the Valley Director. Turn those events into quest offers using authored templates. Check that the people, objectives, routes, and rewards exist before offering a quest.

5. Reuse the framework. Prove it in P300 first, then reuse the world data and tools for other RPG regions or projects. Keep Godot as the foundation and use C++ where profiling shows it will help.

comments.author: TheBigQuestion354
comments.body:
I am making a DnD style RPG so I feel I can give some feedback.  
First: IF you are genuinly interested in this idea get off the potato. I started on a potato and upgraded to a 5070 with 64GB of RAM and a decent CPU and it's insane not just the quality difference but also how much work you can get done in parallel.  
Second: Download and use free textures.  
Third: Do not make walls, terrian, etc. "in code". They should be real models which takes more effort but is worth it.  
Fourth: This is purely a suggestion, try to put a unique style on it because right now it looks a bit like I told Claude to make exactly what you're trying to make. If you want it to look good, one of the most important steps is "Designing" your style to avoid the generic outputs that AI normally gives.
